notes: Only 3 of the 25 checks separate the two configurations; the other 22 pass with and without the skill. The baseline model is already strong at IA basics (merging duplicate tags, cutting the sidebar to six items, mapping every URL), so these checks mostly confirm a floor rather than measure the skill.

Where the skill shows, it is in rigour more than in the headline answer: with the skill, runs tested each alternative scheme against all 24 posts before choosing, named one canonical home for export and invite, wrote tree-test tasks with correct answers and numeric targets, and gave every sitemap node a template type plus a 15-template content model. The baseline sidebar and blog runs reached similar structures but without those.

The one with-skill failure is caused by the skill's own advice: it left the off-audience freelance pricing post unlisted with no category, although the prompt asked for a category for every post, and then contradicted itself ('0 posts without a category', 'category required, exactly one'). Fix: place every item the user asks to place, give a misfit its least-bad home, and argue for removing it separately.

Cost: with the skill, runs took about 58% longer (631s vs 398s) and used about 21% more tokens; deliverables were 20 to 80% longer. Some of that length is the extra validation and content-model work; some is verbosity worth trimming.
One run per configuration, so the 4-point pass-rate gap is within noise; read the outputs, not the delta.
